dept.name: Department of Biotechnology
dept.tagline: The whole 136-credit BSc in Biotechnology as BRACU prints it - core, four labs, 20 electives, the 12-week attachment and the two-semester thesis - with a lab-first toolkit and a tracker on BRACU's scale.
dept.contact: See the Department of Biotechnology page on bracu.ac.bd for the current contact
skills: Year 1
A lab notebook from the first week of BTE 105 Biotech Lab I: dated, in ink, every gel and plate labelled.
Standard solutions, titrations and the balance (the Lab I description) done until the arithmetic is automatic.
Biology and biochemistry as one picture (BIO 101, BCH 101, BTE 101, BTE 102, BTE 103).
The 30 / 20 / 50 marks split of every theory course understood - and the 70% attendance floor never tested.
Year 2
Enzyme kinetics with real numbers (BCH 202) and metabolism you can draw (BTE 202).
Molecular biology at the bench: DNA isolation, gel electrophoresis and PCR in BTE 205 and BTE 208 alongside BTE 203 and BTE 204.
Spectrophotometry and the Beer-Lambert calculation on your own data.
One outside-major course chosen on purpose - statistics (STA 201 then BTE 317) or programming (CSE 110) pay back in Year 4.
Year 3
Microbial, environmental and industrial biotechnology (BTE 302, 304, 306) with the fermentation and bioreactor work of BTE 305.
SDS-PAGE and immunodiffusion done cleanly (BTE 303, BTE 305); plant biotechnology (BTE 308).
Two electives that point the same way (tool 1), and a faculty member who knows your name.
Three papers read with the matrix (tool 7) in the area you want to spend Year 4 on.
Year 4
BTE 450: a supervisor, a question, a notebook of real data, the 7th-semester viva and the 8th-semester defence.
Bioinformatics you can show (BTE 401, BTE 409): one analysis a stranger can rerun.
BTE 400: 12 weeks inside a firm and a training report the host signs.
A one-page CV, a clean lab-skills list and two recommenders who have seen you at the bench.
dept.career_intro: The programme page names the kinds of organisations its students have worked with - ICDDR,B, ACI, INCEPTA, ideSHi, BARI, NIB and BCSIR as collaborators, and ICDDR,B, IEDCR, CHRF, NIPSOM, NIB, BCSIR and NGRI as off-campus internship and research hosts - and BRACU's own MSc in Biotechnology as a next step. The directions below are the common ones; none is a BRACU rule.
careers: Research and higher study
A master's or PhD in biotechnology, molecular biology, genomics or bioinformatics, in Bangladesh or abroad.
CGPA, a BTE 450 thesis with a defensible result, a poster or paper, two recommenders who know your bench work.
Pharmaceutical and vaccine industry
Production, quality control, R&D and regulatory work where biology meets GMP.
BTE 302, 306, 404 (bioprocess), BTE 310 Medical Biotechnology; a BTE 400 attachment in a pharmaceutical firm.
Diagnostics and clinical laboratories
Molecular diagnostics, DNA fingerprinting, immunoassays.
BTE 403, BTE 303 and BTE 405, PCR and SDS-PAGE done cleanly, a Protocols sheet full of ticks.
Food, agriculture and aquaculture
Fermentation, crop and livestock biotechnology, fisheries, food safety.
BTE 309, 311, 314, 408; the fermentation runs of Biotech Lab IV; a project with a real producer.
Environment and energy
Bioremediation, waste treatment, biofuels.
BTE 304, BTE 313, 315, 407; ENV 103 as an outside-major course.
Bioinformatics and data
Sequence analysis, genomics pipelines, computational biology.
BTE 401, BTE 409, BTE 312, BTE 317 Biostatistics after STA 201, CSE 110; one analysis published on your GitHub.
Biotech enterprise and policy
Start-ups, IPR, biosafety regulation, science communication.
BTE 415 Entrepreneurship in Biotechnology, BTE 412 IPR, BTE 402 GMOs and Biosafety, BTE 414; the Entrepreneurship Forum.
Teaching and public health
Schools, colleges, NGOs and research institutes that need biologists who can run a lab.
Every lab course, BTE 316 Social Impact of Biotechnology, a clear explanation of your thesis to a non-scientist.
career_notes: The programme page says a student can take a double major with Biotechnology as the first major, or Biotechnology as a minor. The Minor in Biotechnology page lists 21 credits of core (BCH 101, BCH 202, BTE 101, BTE 103, BTE 203, BTE 204, BTE 304) and 6 of electives (BTE 415, 417, 315, 313, 416), each with in-built lab exercises; the Double Major page (for Microbiology students) asks for 15 extra credits, 151 in all, with the internship and thesis on a topic related to one or both majors. Neither page prints a CGPA rule or an application step - ask the department office.

The page calls the programme '4-year (12 semesters)' but its semester table prints eight semesters, two a year, with no Summer semester placed. Your advising sheet decides where the Summer semesters go; the eight-semester plan is printed in Part 1 as the page prints it.

rules.standing_note: Standing uses BRACU's published rule (from Summer 2022): a CGPA below 2.00 means probation for the following semester, with up to three consecutive semesters to climb back (two for Pharmacy and LL.B). rules.retake_note: BRACU's published rules (read Oct 2026): after an F a course may be retaken twice (a third time by exception of the Head or Dean) and the policy page says the best grade counts; a passed course may be repeated once within two semesters of first enrolment and the latest grade counts. The separate retake-and-repeat page caps a retaken or repeated course at B+ and limits repeats to grades of B- or below. A retake or repeat in the previous or current semester also makes you ineligible for the merit waiver. Weigh that before you repeat a passing grade.

facts: The programme page states "The total credit requirements for the degree of Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology are 136" and describes it as "A 4-year (12 semesters) biotechnology undergraduate program", although its semester table prints eight semesters (two per year).
Fall and Spring semesters are 14 weeks and the Summer semester is 9 weeks; one credit hour is one 60-minute class per week over a 14-week semester.

BTE 450 Biotech Project (4 credits) runs across the 7th and 8th semesters (2 credits each) under a supervisor who may be BRAC University faculty or an expert from another university, R&D organisation or biotech firm; the student submits a dissertation and defends it before a viva board.
Thesis/Project marks: Viva-Voce (end of the 7th semester) 15, Thesis/Project Work 45, Defence (end of 8th semester) 40, out of 100.
Program Highlights: "students must complete a research project as their thesis work in order to obtain the degree".

BTE 400 Industrial Attachment (3 credits, 8th semester) is 12 weeks of work at a biotechnology firm (food, agriculture, industry or pharmaceuticals), individually or in groups of three, ending in a training report endorsed by the host enterprise and graded by the course teacher.

The four lab courses Biotech Lab I-IV (BTE 105, BTE 205, BTE 208, BTE 305) carry 1.5 credits each (6 in total) and sit in the 1st, 3rd, 4th and 5th semesters; Program Highlights add that "each course in this curriculum includes experiments to conduct as in-class laboratory work".

Lab course marks: Reports/Class Tests/Participation/Viva-Voce 30, Lab Experiments 30, Final Examination 40; theory course marks: Quizzes/Class Tests/Assignments/Participation/Attendance 30, Mid Term Examination 20, Final Examination (comprehensive)/Projects 50.

Attendance is worth 5 marks in every course (90% and above = 5, 85-<90 = 4, 80-<85 = 3, 75-<80 = 2, 70-<75 = 1, below 70 = 0) and a student who attends less than 70% of classes, tutorials and labs is not allowed to sit the final examination.
ENG 091 Foundation Course is non-credit and "The student may also be required to take non-credit remedial course in English".
"For elective and outside major courses a student can choose from several courses outlined in the syllabus in consultation with the department."

Students can take a double major with Biotechnology as the first major, or Biotechnology as a minor; the Minor in Biotechnology page lists 21 credits of core courses (BCH 101, BCH 202, BTE 101, BTE 103, BTE 203, BTE 204, BTE 304) plus 6 credits of electives (BTE 415, BTE 417, BTE 315, BTE 313, BTE 416), each with in-built lab exercises.

The Double Major in Biotechnology page (for BS in Microbiology students) requires 15 extra credits for a total of 151, with the internship and thesis topics related to one or both majors and no extra biotechnology lab courses.

Tuition and Fees page, "All other Program" row: Tk 8,250 per credit, semester fee Tk 10,520, admission fee Tk 33,900 (one time, non-refundable), library membership fee Tk 2,500 (one time, non-refundable), freshman course fee Tk 24,750 per course; "Fees can be changed as per the decision of the university."

book.text: Read this first

This planner puts your whole Biotechnology degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.
What you are holding

items: **Degree** - the Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology as BRACU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on BRACU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - BRACU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.

book.text: What it is not

items: It is **not an official BRACU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from BRACU's own web pages on 20 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.

book.text: Start in 15 minutes

items: On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Your data

Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

items: I have saved a copy with my data inside once, so I know where the button is.

the Rules tab - Rules that move your CGPA and your money

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from BRAC University's published pages as they stood in October 2026; the source is named under each section.
The grading scale
BRAC University's undergraduate scale, in force since Fall 2020. Both A+ and A carry the full 4.0.
A+ to D- are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA. The policy page prints the same formula: the sum of (grade points x credits) over the credits attempted.
Three things students get wrong

items: **An F stays in the sum until it is retaken.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top.
**A D- passes, but it costs you.** A 3-credit D- is 2.1 quality points against 12.0 for an A - and a grade of B- or below is what the repeat rule exists for.
**W, I, P and AU never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

2. The marks map: 30 / 20 / 50, 30 / 30 / 40, and the 70% floor

The programme page prints how every course is marked. Theory: **30** for quizzes, class tests, assignments, participation and attendance, **20** for the mid-term, **50** for the comprehensive final or project. Lab: **30** for reports, class tests, participation and viva, **30** for the lab experiments, **40** for the final. Attendance is **5 marks** of the first 30 on a ladder (90% and above = 5, 85-<90 = 4, 80-<85 = 3, 75-<80 = 2, 70-<75 = 1, below 70 = 0), and **below 70% attendance you are not allowed to sit the final**. Most marks are lost before the final paper, in the 30 nobody plans for.

3. A lab notebook that survives the viva

The four labs - **BTE 105 Biotech Lab I, BTE 205 Lab II, BTE 208 Lab III, BTE 305 Lab IV**, 1.5 credits each - carry 30 marks for reports, class tests, participation and viva, 30 for the experiments and 40 for the final. The Course Details describe each lab as practicals based on the theory courses of its level, from balances and titrations in Lab I to fermentation, SDS-PAGE and immunodiffusion in Lab IV. A notebook is a record written while you work: if an entry would not let a classmate repeat your work, it is not finished.

items: Write **as you go**, in pen, with the date on every page. Never tear a page out; strike through mistakes with one line.
Record **what you actually did**, including the pipetting error and the tube you dropped - deviations explain results.
Paste or sketch every gel, plate and printout, **labelled lane by lane**.
End every entry with **what the result means and what you will do next** - the sentence the viva examiner asks for.

rows: Mass to weigh for a molar solution
mass (g) = molarity (mol/L) x volume (L) x molar mass (g/mol)
C1 x V1 = C2 x V2
10 mL of 1x from a 50x stock: V1 = 1 x 10 / 50 = 0.2 mL stock + 9.8 mL diluent
% w/v = grams per 100 mL;  % v/v = mL per 100 mL
A = e x c x l, so c = A / (e x l)
each step multiplies the dilution factor

items: Lab coat on and closed; closed shoes; long hair tied; gloves changed when contaminated - and off before touching phones, doors or my face.

BTE 403, BTE 303 and BTE 405, PCR and SDS-PAGE done cleanly, a Protocols sheet full of ticks.
Fermentation, crop and livestock biotechnology, fisheries, food safety.
BTE 309, 311, 314, 408; the fermentation runs of Biotech Lab IV; a project with a real producer.
BTE 304, BTE 313, 315, 407; ENV 103 as an outside-major course.
Sequence analysis, genomics pipelines, computational biology.
BTE 401, BTE 409, BTE 312, BTE 317 Biostatistics after STA 201, CSE 110; one analysis published on your GitHub.
Start-ups, IPR, biosafety regulation, science communication.
BTE 415 Entrepreneurship in Biotechnology, BTE 412 IPR, BTE 402 GMOs and Biosafety, BTE 414; the Entrepreneurship Forum.
Schools, colleges, NGOs and research institutes that need biologists who can run a lab.
Every lab course, BTE 316 Social Impact of Biotechnology, a clear explanation of your thesis to a non-scientist.

book.title: Minor and double major
items: The programme page says a student can take a double major with Biotechnology as the first major, or Biotechnology as a minor. The Minor in Biotechnology page lists 21 credits of core (BCH 101, BCH 202, BTE 101, BTE 103, BTE 203, BTE 204, BTE 304) and 6 of electives (BTE 415, 417, 315, 313, 416), each with in-built lab exercises; the Double Major page (for Microbiology students) asks for 15 extra credits, 151 in all, with the internship and thesis on a topic related to one or both majors. Neither page prints a CGPA rule or an application step - ask the department office.

book.title: Eight semesters or twelve
items: The page calls the programme '4-year (12 semesters)' but its semester table prints eight semesters, two a year, with no Summer semester placed. Your advising sheet decides where the Summer semesters go; the eight-semester plan is printed in the Degree tab as the page prints it.
